sets.title: Small parks, big effects
sets.intro: 城市绿地：小而分散的公园是否比一个大公园更有价值。8 题（4 选择 / 2 判断 / 2 填空），建议 15 分钟。
sets.passage:
A. For most of the twentieth century, city planners treated green space as decoration: something pleasant to look at, usually placed in one large park at the edge of the city. In the last decade a different idea has taken hold. Small, scattered parks, it is argued, may matter more than one grand one, because what determines whether people use a park is how far they have to walk to reach it.

B. Pocket parks are plots smaller than a tennis court, often built on vacant lots between buildings. They are cheap to create and quick to open. Research across three European cities found that residents living within 300 metres of a pocket park used it, on average, four times a week. Those who lived near a large park two kilometres away visited it less than once a week. Distance, not size, predicted use.

C. The benefits reach beyond recreation. A study of forty neighbourhoods reported measurably lower summer temperatures within 200 metres of new planting, and storm water absorption also improved, because soil and roots hold rain that would otherwise run into drains and flood streets during heavy storms.

D. Not every scheme works. Where parks were built without consulting the people who would use them, vandalism rose and planting was pulled out within a year. Critics also point to maintenance. A park needs watering, pruning and cleaning, and a small park is not necessarily cheaper per visitor than a large one, since fixed costs are spread across fewer people. Cities that have succeeded tend to fund upkeep with a small levy on local businesses and to hand day-to-day management to residents' committees, which notice damage quickly.

E. The lesson is not that small is always better. It is that a measured approach - testing several sites, measuring how people actually use them, and being willing to change course when the evidence points elsewhere - produces better results than a single flagship project that looks impressive in a photograph.

questions.prompt: What is the main change described in paragraph A?
options: Cities are building fewer parks than before
Planners now value many small parks over one large park
Park design has become more expensive
Residents prefer parks built outside the city
answers: Planners now value many small parks over one large park
questions.explain: A 段说过去把绿地当装饰、通常放在城边一个大公园里；最近十年「小而分散可能比一个大公园更重要」的新想法占了上风。
questions.explain_en: Paragraph A says planners once treated green space as decoration in one large park at the edge of the city; in the last decade the idea that many small, scattered parks matter more has taken hold.

questions.prompt: What did the European research find?
options: Large parks are used more often than small ones
How far people live from a park predicts how often they use it
Small parks are used mainly by children
The size of a park matters more than its location
answers: How far people live from a park predicts how often they use it
questions.explain: B 段结尾一句：Distance, not size, predicted use（决定使用频率的是距离，不是面积）。
questions.explain_en: Paragraph B ends: 'Distance, not size, predicted use' — how far people live from a park predicts how often they use it.

questions.prompt: According to paragraph C, which benefit was actually measured?
options: Higher property prices near new planting
Lower summer temperatures near new planting
Fewer traffic accidents in those neighbourhoods
Better indoor air quality in nearby buildings
answers: Lower summer temperatures near new planting
questions.explain: C 段只写了两个可测量结果：夏季气温更低、雨水吸纳更好。房价、交通事故、室内空气质量都没提。
questions.explain_en: Paragraph C reports only two measured results: lower summer temperatures and better storm water absorption; property prices, accidents and indoor air are not mentioned.

questions.prompt: What does the writer say about maintenance costs?
options: Small parks are always cheaper to run
Maintenance is paid for entirely by residents
A small park may cost more per visitor than a large one
Maintenance is not a serious concern
answers: A small park may cost more per visitor than a large one
questions.explain: D 段：not necessarily cheaper per visitor，因为固定成本摊到的人更少。
questions.explain_en: Paragraph D: a small park is 'not necessarily cheaper per visitor' because fixed costs are spread across fewer people.

questions.prompt: Residents were always consulted before a park was built.
questions.explain: D 段明确说，在没有征求使用者意见的地方，破坏行为上升、种下的植物一年内被拔掉 —— 并非「总是征求过意见」。
questions.explain_en: Paragraph D says that where parks were built without consulting the people who would use them, vandalism rose — so residents were not always consulted.

questions.prompt: Storm water absorption improved near new planting.
questions.explain: C 段：storm water absorption also improved，与题干一致。
questions.explain_en: Paragraph C: 'storm water absorption also improved', matching the statement.

questions.prompt: Successful cities fund upkeep with a small ______ on local businesses.
questions.explain: D 段原文：fund upkeep with a small levy on local businesses。
questions.explain_en: Paragraph D: 'fund upkeep with a small levy on local businesses'.

questions.prompt: The writer recommends testing several sites and being willing to ______ course.
questions.explain: E 段：being willing to change course when the evidence points elsewhere。
questions.explain_en: Paragraph E: 'being willing to change course when the evidence points elsewhere'.

sets.title: Working from anywhere: who really benefits?
sets.intro: 远程办公六年后的真实得失，含 1 道 NOT GIVEN 判断题。8 题（4 选择 / 2 判断 / 2 填空），建议 15 分钟。
sets.passage:
A. When offices closed in 2020, working from home was an emergency measure adopted in a week. Six years on it has become a settled part of working life in many industries, but the benefits are far from evenly shared, and the argument about it is often conducted as if everyone were in the same position.

B. For an employee with a spare room, a stable connection and no small children at home, remote work is a clear gain. One large survey put the time saved on commuting at seventy-two minutes a day. What is striking is how that time is used: it goes largely into sleep, family and exercise rather than into extra work, which may explain why productivity has not fallen as sharply as some managers predicted.

C. For those in crowded or shared housing, the same arrangement brings constant interruption, higher energy bills and a boundary between work and home that blurs until neither feels finished. In many households the burden of childcare still falls unevenly, and it is usually the lower-paid partner who reduces hours or leaves the labour market altogether.

D. Employers report mixed results. Individual tasks that need concentration - writing, analysis, coding - are often completed faster at home. Work that depends on negotiation, training or mentoring does less well, and younger staff in particular lose the informal learning that happens simply by overhearing a more experienced colleague.

E. The compromise most organisations have reached - two or three days in the office - is less a principled solution than a balance of competing pressures. What the evidence does suggest is that the number of days matters less than two other things: whether a team agrees in advance on when it will be together, and whether managers judge output rather than hours visible on screen.

questions.prompt: What does the writer say about the time saved by not commuting?
options: It is mostly turned into extra work
It goes largely into sleep, family and exercise
answers: It goes largely into sleep, family and exercise
questions.explain: B 段：goes largely into sleep, family and exercise rather than into extra work。
questions.explain_en: Paragraph B: the saved time 'goes largely into sleep, family and exercise rather than into extra work'.

questions.prompt: Which group does the writer identify as most disadvantaged by remote work?
options: People in crowded or shared housing
Employees who have a spare room
Staff who travel to work by train
answers: People in crowded or shared housing
questions.explain: C 段：crowded or shared housing → 持续打扰、电费上升、工作与家庭界限模糊。
questions.explain_en: Paragraph C: people in 'crowded or shared housing' face constant interruption and higher bills.

questions.prompt: Which kind of work is said to suffer when done at home?
questions.explain: D 段：写作、分析、编程在家更快；依赖协商、培训、带教的工作表现更差。
questions.explain_en: Paragraph D: negotiation, training and mentoring do less well, while writing, analysis and coding are faster at home.

questions.prompt: According to paragraph E, what matters most?
options: The exact number of days spent in the office
Teams agreeing on shared days and managers judging output
A return to five days a week in the office
answers: Teams agreeing on shared days and managers judging output
questions.explain: E 段：the number of days matters less than two other things —— 团队提前约定共同在场日、管理者看产出而不是屏幕在线时长。
questions.explain_en: Paragraph E: the number of days matters less than teams agreeing shared days and managers judging output rather than hours on screen.

questions.prompt: The figure of seventy-two minutes comes from employees' own estimates.
questions.explain: 原文只说 One large survey put the time saved at seventy-two minutes a day，没说这是员工自报还是实测 —— 无从判断，选 NOT GIVEN。
questions.explain_en: The text only says a survey put the time at seventy-two minutes; it does not say whether this was self-reported or measured.

questions.prompt: Tasks that need concentration are often completed more quickly at home.
questions.explain: D 段：Individual tasks that need concentration … are often completed faster at home。
questions.explain_en: Paragraph D: tasks that need concentration are 'often completed faster at home'.

questions.prompt: Younger staff lose the informal learning that comes from ______ a more experienced colleague.
questions.explain: D 段原文：by overhearing a more experienced colleague。
questions.explain_en: Paragraph D: informal learning 'by overhearing a more experienced colleague'.

questions.prompt: The two-or-three-day pattern is described as a balance of competing ______.
questions.explain: E 段：less a principled solution than a balance of competing pressures。
questions.explain_en: Paragraph E: 'a balance of competing pressures'.

sets.title: Joining the community library
sets.intro: 电话咨询办理借书证。先听音频（可 0.75–1.5 倍速、可重播），再作答。6 题（4 填空 / 2 选择），音频约 80 秒。
sets.transcript:
Good morning, Riverside Community Library. How can I help you?

Hello. I'd like to join the library. Could you tell me what I need to bring?

Of course. You need one form of identification that shows your address, such as a driving licence or a recent utility bill. Membership itself is free.

Great. And what are your opening hours?

On weekdays we open at nine in the morning and close at eight in the evening. On Saturdays we close earlier, at five. We're closed on Sundays.

Do you have a children's section?

Yes, the children's room is on the second floor. Story time runs every Wednesday afternoon at half past three.

Perfect. Is there anywhere I can study quietly?

We have a silent study room on the first floor, next to the newspapers. It has twenty desks, but you can't book them - it's first come, first served.

That's fine. One more thing - can I borrow DVDs?

Yes. DVDs can be borrowed for one week, and the late fee is fifty pence per day.

questions.explain: 原文：one form of identification that shows your address。驾照或近期的水电账单都可以。
questions.explain_en: The clerk says you need 'one form of identification that shows your address'.

questions.prompt: On Saturdays the library closes at ______ p.m.
questions.explain: 原文：On Saturdays we close earlier, at five。工作日是九点到晚上八点，周日闭馆。
questions.explain_en: 'On Saturdays we close earlier, at five' — weekdays are nine to eight, closed on Sundays.

questions.prompt: Where is the children's room?
questions.explain: 原文：the children's room is on the second floor。注意 silent study room 才在一楼。
questions.explain_en: The children's room is on the second floor; the silent study room is on the first floor.

questions.prompt: Story time takes place on Wednesday afternoons at ______.
questions.explain: 原文：Story time runs every Wednesday afternoon at half past three。
questions.explain_en: 'Story time runs every Wednesday afternoon at half past three'.

questions.prompt: How can you get a desk in the silent study room?
questions.explain: 原文：you can't book them — it's first come, first served（先到先得）。
questions.explain_en: You can't book a desk — 'it's first come, first served'.

questions.prompt: DVDs can be borrowed for ______.
questions.explain: 原文：DVDs can be borrowed for one week，逾期费每天五十便士。
questions.explain_en: 'DVDs can be borrowed for one week', with a late fee of fifty pence a day.

sets.title: Why we waste a third of the food we grow
sets.intro: 粮食浪费的成因与代价，含 1 道 NOT GIVEN 判断题。8 题（4 选择 / 2 判断 / 2 填空），建议 15 分钟。
sets.passage:
A. Roughly one-third of all food produced for human consumption is never eaten. Where that waste happens depends on income. In wealthy countries most of it occurs at the end of the chain - in supermarkets and in homes - while in poorer ones food is lost closer to the farm, to pests, poor storage and a lack of refrigeration.

B. Supermarkets are frequently blamed, and with some reason. Fruit and vegetables that are perfectly edible are rejected for cosmetic reasons, and 'buy one get one free' offers encourage households to buy more than they will eat. Date labels add to the confusion: the distinction between 'best before', which is about quality, and 'use by', which is about safety, is widely misunderstood. Many people throw food away on the best-before date even when it is perfectly safe.

C. Homes are the single largest source of food waste in rich countries, ahead of farms, factories and shops. One cause is portion size: recipes and packaging push people to cook too much. Another is planning - shoppers often buy without checking what they already have, so ingredients are forgotten at the back of the fridge until they have spoiled.

D. The costs are not only moral. Wasted food means wasted water, land and fuel, and rotting food in landfill releases methane, a greenhouse gas that is far more potent than carbon dioxide in the short term. Some governments have responded by requiring supermarkets to donate unsold edible food to charities rather than bin it; others have funded campaigns teaching the difference between the two date labels.

E. Experts argue that the biggest gains come from small, repeated habits rather than grand schemes: writing a list before shopping, using the freezer, and cooking one more meal from leftovers before buying again. As one researcher puts it, we do not need everyone to become perfect - we need everyone to waste a little less, a little more often.

questions.prompt: In wealthy countries, where does most food waste happen?
questions.explain: A 段：在富裕国家，大部分浪费发生在链条末端——超市和家里；在穷国则是靠近农场的地方。
questions.explain_en: Paragraph A: in wealthy countries most waste happens at the end of the chain — in supermarkets and in homes.

questions.prompt: Why are the two date labels a problem?
options: They mean exactly the same thing
People misunderstand them and throw away safe food
They are too expensive for small producers to print
They are only printed in one language
answers: People misunderstand them and throw away safe food
questions.explain: B 段：best before 关乎品质、use by 关乎安全，两者常被误解，很多人过了 best-before 日期就扔掉其实仍安全可吃的食物。
questions.explain_en: 'best before' is about quality and 'use by' is about safety; the difference is widely misunderstood, so safe food gets thrown away.

questions.prompt: What is the single largest source of food waste in rich countries?
questions.explain: C 段开头：Homes are the single largest source of food waste in rich countries。
questions.explain_en: Paragraph C opens: 'Homes are the single largest source of food waste in rich countries'.

questions.prompt: Why is rotting food in landfill harmful?
options: It consumes too much paper for packaging
It attracts insects that spread disease
questions.explain: D 段：腐烂食物在填埋场释放甲烷，短期内远比二氧化碳更强的温室气体。
questions.explain_en: Paragraph D: rotting food releases methane, far more potent than carbon dioxide in the short term.

questions.prompt: In poorer countries, most food is lost near the farm, for example to pests or poor storage.
questions.explain: A 段：在穷国食物损失更靠近农场，原因是虫害、储存条件差、缺少冷藏。
questions.explain_en: Paragraph A: in poorer countries food is lost closer to the farm, to pests, poor storage and a lack of refrigeration.

questions.prompt: Fruit that looks imperfect is less nutritious than fruit that looks perfect.
questions.explain: B 段只说不完美的蔬果因外观被拒收，没比较营养价值，营养高低无从判断。
questions.explain_en: Paragraph B only says imperfect produce is rejected for cosmetic reasons; it never compares nutritional value.

questions.prompt: Rotting food releases ______, a gas more potent than carbon dioxide in the short term.
questions.explain: D 段原文：releases methane, a greenhouse gas … far more potent than carbon dioxide in the short term。
questions.explain_en: Paragraph D: 'releases methane ... far more potent than carbon dioxide in the short term'.

questions.prompt: Experts recommend cooking ______ from leftovers before shopping again.
questions.explain: E 段：cooking one more meal from leftovers before buying again。
questions.explain_en: Paragraph E: 'cooking one more meal from leftovers before buying again'.

sets.title: Wortham Museum re-opening
sets.intro: 博物馆重开通知（独白）。先听音频，再作答。6 题（4 填空 / 2 选择），音频约 75 秒。
sets.transcript:
Welcome back to Wortham Museum. After two years of rebuilding, we are opening our doors again on Saturday the fourteenth of June. The old clock tower gallery has been restored, and we have added a new cafe and a lift, so every floor is now wheelchair accessible.

Admission is free for under-sixteens and for members, but everyone else pays six pounds fifty. If you plan to visit regularly, an annual membership costs twenty-four pounds, which works out cheaper after just four visits.

Our new exhibition, Voices of the Mill, tells the story of the town's textile workers. It runs from the fourteenth of June until the end of September, and guided tours leave the entrance every hour on the hour from ten until four.

Please note that the car park behind the museum now closes at six in the evening, and it is free for the first two hours only. The easiest way to reach us is the number seven bus, which stops directly outside.

We look forward to seeing you.

questions.explain: 原文：we are opening our doors again on Saturday the fourteenth of June。
questions.explain_en: 'We are opening our doors again on Saturday the fourteenth of June'.

questions.explain: 原文：Admission is free for under-sixteens and for members。
questions.explain_en: 'Admission is free for under-sixteens and for members'.

questions.explain: 原文：an annual membership costs twenty-four pounds，四次就回本。
questions.explain_en: 'An annual membership costs twenty-four pounds', cheaper after four visits.

questions.explain_en: 'Guided tours leave the entrance every hour on the hour from ten until four'.

questions.explain: 原文：the car park behind the museum now closes at six in the evening。

questions.explain: 原文：the number seven bus, which stops directly outside。
questions.explain_en: 'The number seven bus ... stops directly outside'.

sets.title: Booking a careers appointment
sets.intro: 电话预约职业中心改简历。先听音频（可 0.75–1.5 倍速、可重播），再作答。6 题（4 填空 / 1 选择 / 1 判断），音频约 60 秒。
sets.transcript: Good morning, this is the university Careers Centre. How can I help you? Hello. I would like to book an appointment to have my CV checked, please. Certainly. We have slots on Tuesday afternoon or Thursday morning. Which do you prefer? Thursday morning, please. That is Thursday at ten thirty. The appointment lasts thirty minutes. Could I take your student number? Yes, it is S double four seven two. Thank you. Please bring a printed copy of your CV and a list of three jobs you are interested in. Do I need to bring my passport? No, just your student card. One more thing. Do you run practice interviews? Yes, on Friday afternoons. They are free, but you must book a week in advance. Great, I will do that. Thank you.

questions.explain: 原文：The appointment lasts thirty minutes。
questions.explain_en: The appointment lasts 30 minutes.

questions.prompt: Students should bring a printed CV and a list of ______ jobs they are interested in.
questions.explain: 原文：a list of three jobs you are interested in。
questions.explain_en: Bring a printed CV and a list of three jobs.

sets.intro: 讲座片段：城市绿地对压力的影响（独白）。6 题（4 填空 / 1 选择 / 1 判断），音频约 65 秒。
sets.transcript: Today I want to talk about urban green spaces. Research from the University of Manchester found that people who live within three hundred metres of a park report lower levels of stress. The effect was strongest among residents over sixty. However, the study also showed that the size of the park mattered less than its quality. A small, well maintained garden with seats and paths was more beneficial than a large field with no facilities. The researchers recommend that cities spend at least five percent of their transport budget on walking routes to parks. In the Netherlands, one city has already converted ten percent of its car parks into small gardens, and cycling to local shops increased by a third.

questions.explain_en: A small well-maintained garden beats a large field with no facilities.

sets.transcript:
[Section 1: Student accommodation]
Good morning, City Housing Office. How can I help? I would like to register for student accommodation. Certainly. Could I have your name and student number? Maria Lopez, student number four four seven one. Thank you. Which campus are you studying at? The north campus. We have rooms at three halls. Riverside is the closest, but it is full until December. Green Court has rooms from September, and it is a ten minute bus ride. How much is Green Court? A single room is four hundred and eighty pounds a month, including internet but not electricity. Is there a deposit? Yes, three hundred pounds, refundable at the end of your contract. Can I see a room this week? We have viewings on Wednesday at two and Friday at eleven. Wednesday at two, please. Great. Please bring your student card and a bank statement.

[Section 2: Community festival]
Welcome to the Riverside Community Festival. The festival runs from Friday the fifth to Sunday the seventh of June. Most events are free, but the evening concert on Saturday costs eight pounds, and tickets can be bought at the library or online. The main stage is in the park next to the river. The craft market is in the town hall, and children's activities are in the school playground. Parking is available at the station car park, which is a five minute walk from the park. Please note that the park gates close at ten in the evening. Volunteers should report to the information tent thirty minutes before their shift. Lost property will be kept at the town hall.

[Section 3: Research discussion]
So, have you decided on your research topic? I am thinking about urban cycling, but the data might be hard to collect. That is true. What about using the city's traffic survey? They publish counts every year. I did not know that. That would save a lot of time. I am more interested in how weather affects commuting. I could use the same survey. Good, but be careful with correlation. You would need at least three years of data. I was planning to use five. Excellent. Anna, if you use the survey, focus on one district rather than the whole city. The north district has the most cycle lanes. Perfect. Submit your proposal by the fifteenth of next month.

[Section 4: Sleep and memory]
Today's lecture is about sleep and memory. Researchers at the University of Leeds asked two hundred students to learn a list of words, either in the morning or in the evening. Students who learned in the evening and slept before testing remembered twenty percent more words. The effect was strongest for factual information rather than skills. Sleep appears to help the brain transfer memories from short term to long term storage. However, the researchers stress that the quality of sleep matters more than the quantity. Participants who woke up several times during the night showed almost no benefit. The team recommends avoiding caffeine after four in the afternoon and keeping the bedroom cool, around eighteen degrees.

sets.title: Can cities grow their own food?
sets.intro: 城市农业：垂直农场与屋顶农场的收益和代价。8 题（4 选择 / 2 判断 / 2 填空），建议 15 分钟。
sets.passage:
Urban farming is no longer a hobby. In Singapore, which imports more than 90% of its food, the government has set a target of producing 30% locally by 2030. Rooftop farms now supply vegetables to supermarkets, and vertical farms use LED lighting to grow leafy greens in stacks up to ten metres high.

Supporters argue that urban farms shorten supply chains, reduce transport emissions and give city dwellers access to fresher produce. Critics point out that the energy used by indoor farms can make their vegetables more carbon-intensive than those trucked in from the countryside. A study from the National University of Singapore found that lettuce grown in a climate-controlled vertical farm used about three times as much electricity per kilogram as field-grown lettuce.

The researchers suggest that urban farms should focus on crops that travel badly, such as herbs and soft fruit, rather than staples like rice. They also recommend using renewable energy and sharing facilities between farms to cut costs. Singapore's target is ambitious, but the debate shows that growing food in cities is less about technology than about choosing the right crops and the right energy.

questions.explain_en: Singapore imports over 90% of its food.

questions.explain: 原文：producing 30% locally by 2030。
questions.explain_en: The target is 30% by 2030.

questions.explain_en: Crops that travel badly, such as herbs and soft fruit.

sets.title: The four-day week experiment
sets.intro: 四天工作制试验：结果与局限。8 题（4 选择 / 2 判断 / 2 填空），建议 15 分钟。
sets.passage:
In 2022, more than 60 companies in the UK took part in a six-month trial of a four-day working week with no cut in pay. Employees worked 80% of their usual hours but were expected to maintain full productivity. At the end of the trial, 56 of the 61 companies said they would continue with the shorter week, and 18 made it permanent.

Staff reported lower stress and fewer sick days, while revenue stayed broadly the same. However, the trial had limitations. Most participating companies were small, and many were in the service sector, where productivity is difficult to measure. Critics argue that the results may not apply to hospitals, factories or schools, where shifts must be covered.

Some companies that continued the policy introduced longer working days, from eight hours to ten, which employees found tiring. The researchers concluded that the four-day week can work, but only where managers are willing to cut meetings and redesign workflows. Shorter hours, in other words, require a different way of working rather than simply squeezing five days into four.

questions.explain: 原文：a six-month trial。
questions.explain_en: The trial lasted six months.

questions.explain: 原文：worked 80% of their usual hours。
questions.explain_en: They worked 80% of usual hours.

questions.explain: 原文：56 of the 61 companies said they would continue，其中 18 家永久化。
questions.explain_en: 56 of 61 would continue; 18 made it permanent.

sets.title: Why plastic recycling is so difficult
sets.intro: 塑料回收率低的原因与政策方向。8 题（4 选择 / 2 判断 / 2 填空），建议 15 分钟。
sets.passage:
Only about 9% of the plastic ever produced has been recycled. The rest has been burned, buried or left in the environment. One reason is that plastic is not a single material: there are thousands of types, each with different melting points and additives. Mixing them weakens the recycled product, so sorting is essential but expensive.

In Norway, a deposit scheme for bottles achieves a return rate above 90%, because consumers pay a small deposit that is refunded when they return the container. The scheme works best for drinks containers, which are made of a few standard plastics. For packaging such as films and pouches, which are often layered with other materials, recycling remains difficult.

Some companies are now designing packaging that uses a single material, and the EU has proposed rules requiring all packaging to be recyclable by 2030. Researchers argue that the most effective policy is to reduce packaging altogether rather than rely on recycling. As one engineer put it, the best plastic is the plastic that is never made.

sets.title: Saving languages before they vanish
sets.intro: 语言消失与记录技术的作用与局限。8 题（4 选择 / 2 判断 / 2 填空），建议 15 分钟。
sets.passage:
A language dies roughly every two weeks. Of the world's 7,000 languages, about 40% are considered endangered. When a language disappears, knowledge disappears with it: plant names, weather terms and oral histories that were never written down.

Linguists have traditionally recorded languages by writing grammars and dictionaries, but this work is slow and often incomplete. New technology is changing the picture. Smartphones allow speakers to record vocabulary and stories themselves, and machine-learning tools can help transcribe recordings in languages with no written form. In one project in Australia, elders recorded 2,000 hours of speech in a language with fewer than 50 fluent speakers; the resulting archive is now used in schools.

However, researchers warn that technology alone cannot save a language. A language survives only if children learn it at home and in daily life. Policies that support bilingual education and community radio are therefore at least as important as recording. Documentation preserves a language for study; only daily use keeps it alive.

questions.explain: 原文：roughly every two weeks。
questions.explain_en: About every two weeks.

questions.prompt: About ______% of the world's languages are endangered.
questions.explain: 原文：about 40% are considered endangered。
questions.explain_en: About 40%.

options: Plant names, weather terms and oral histories
answers: Plant names, weather terms and oral histories
questions.explain: 原文：knowledge disappears with it: plant names, weather terms and oral histories。
questions.explain_en: Knowledge such as plant names and oral histories.

questions.explain: 原文：this work is slow and often incomplete。
questions.explain_en: It is slow and often incomplete.

questions.explain_en: Transcribe languages with no written form.

questions.explain: 原文：elders recorded 2,000 hours of speech。
questions.explain_en: 2,000 hours of speech.

questions.explain: 原文：technology alone cannot save a language。
questions.explain_en: Technology alone cannot save a language.

questions.explain: 原文：Policies that support bilingual education and community radio are therefore at least as important as recording。
